children: , the mobile advertising platform, fell 3.50% in premarket after Edgewater Research analyst Joe Wittine said fresh channel checks show its market share expansion has effectively stalled. Wittine forecast fourth-quarter revenue growth of just 8% to 9% quarter-over-quarter and found the company's share-of-wallet and share-of-voice metrics are no longer consistently rising from already industry-leading levels.

He tied the slowdown to the MAX network's share hitting a ceiling. Competition is also squeezing AppLovin's net revenue spreads, particularly from Unity Software (U). He also found little evidence that the algorithm update management highlighted on its second-quarter call drove real gains in August, reading the rebound mostly as a recovery from a weak July.

For scale, AppLovin reported $1.92 billion in second-quarter revenue and guided the third quarter to $2.055 billion to $2.085 billion, implying roughly 7% to 8.6% sequential growth. "This has turned into a show-me story," Wittine said, expecting late-2026 and 2027 consensus estimates to move lower before AppLovin's third-quarter report.

title: AppLovin Stock Falls as Edgewater Sees Growth Hitting a Ceiling
